content.value_statement: Adding a Catalyst-Relay endpoint requires matching route, validation, response, client, and documentation patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a concise checklist for implementing endpoints consistently.
actual_capabilities: Defines the route file pattern for Catalyst-Relay endpoint modules.
Shows how to colocate request schemas, response types, and Hono handlers.
Explains route registration in the server route index.
Standardizes success and error response envelopes.
Connects HTTP endpoints to ADTClient library methods when needed.
Lists required endpoint documentation sections and a completion checklist.
limitations: It is tailored to Catalyst-Relay conventions, not every Hono project.
It provides guidance only and does not generate files by itself.
It does not define authentication or authorization policy.
It does not replace project-specific tests or code review.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation and Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with request validation needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an endpoint for [feature] with clear Zod validation, typed success output, validation errors, and consistent response envelopes.

prompt_templates.title: Map Endpoint to Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for server and library mode parity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an endpoint for [feature] and map it to the matching ADTClient method. Include route registration and documentation updates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Endpoint Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before merging an endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Catalyst-Relay endpoint change for route structure, validation, response envelope, client mapping, documentation coverage, and missing tests.

output_examples.input: Request to add a login endpoint.
output_examples.output: A route implementation plan with validation, handler structure, route registration, client mapping, and endpoint documentation tasks.

output_examples.input: Request to review a new package endpoint.
output_examples.output: A consistency review covering request schema, response envelope, error codes, documentation sections, and follow-up test needs.

output_examples.input: Request to document a completed endpoint.
output_examples.output: A documentation outline with request details, response fields, errors, use cases, and library usage guidance.

best_practices: Keep each endpoint in its own route file with colocated schema, types, and handler.
Use consistent success and error envelopes across every endpoint.
Update route wiring, client methods, documentation, and type checks in the same change.
anti_patterns: Do not place endpoint schemas far from the handler that uses them.
Do not return ad hoc response shapes that break client expectations.
Do not add routes without matching documentation and library mapping review.

faq.question: What framework conventions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Catalyst-Relay server routes built with Hono, TypeScript, and Zod validation.

faq.question: Does the skill create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation guidance that an AI coding agent can follow in the project.

faq.question: When should I update ADTClient?
faq.answer: Update ADTClient when the HTTP endpoint wraps functionality that should also be available in library mode.

faq.question: What documentation should a new endpoint include?
faq.answer: Include request details, body fields, response fields, examples, error codes, use cases, and library usage.

faq.question: Can this skill be used with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill define security rules for endpoints?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on route structure and documentation, so project security policy must still be applied.
